extracted.intended_audience: aspiring authors querying literary agents (especially those seeking representation for books/memoirs/nonfiction/YA)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for writers preparing queries, proposals, and manuscripts to attract literary-agent representation, including agent genre preferences, common submission mistakes, platform expectations, and what makes a memoir or nonfiction project attractive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent genre preferences (what he is seeking)
rubrics_metrics.description: He is seeking: Narrative and prescriptive nonfiction, memoir, military, history, diet & fitness, science, as well as young adult.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this list to target queries to appropriate agents; the interview also notes commercial examples he has sold (celebrity memoirs, photo books, etc.) to illustrate the kinds of nonfiction/memoir projects he champions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genres/projects not sought
rubrics_metrics.description: He does not seek: Poetry, screenplays, or YA paranormal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not query this agent with projects in these categories; elsewhere he indicates he may still sell some unexpected genres if commercially viable, but these are explicitly excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing quality and voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Besides 'good writing,' and 'voice,' what agents look for is strong writing and a distinctive voice that draws readers in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good opening, compelling prose, and a clear narrative voice are essential. The agent emphasizes that quality of writing is a primary filter when evaluating submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid writing solely to trends
rubrics_metrics.description: There’s plenty of room for tried and true concepts, but writing to a certain trend, like dystopian, isn’t enough to net a book deal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trend-following manuscripts that clearly exist only to capitalize on a popular category are often rejected; agents prefer original takes or projects with intrinsic merit beyond current fads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memoir-specific desirability
rubrics_metrics.description: A good memoir is a first-person account of a great story that has the power to draw the reader in and keep them reading from cover to cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marketable memoirs tend to be uplifting, tell an inside story of an event, provide an escape, allow readers to go on an adventure with the narrator, or let readers identify with the narrator. Emphasize strong narrative arc and emotional engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial viability
rubrics_metrics.description: The agent will take projects if the writing is of quality and the project is commercially viable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess and present the book’s commercial potential in your proposal—who will buy it, why it will sell now. Exceptional writing can overcome some genre boundaries, but marketability is a key consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query personalization and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Common query mistake: Generic salutations ('Dear Sir or Madam', 'Dear Agent') or addressing the wrong person/agency on the cover letter — those queries get tossed in the trash immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do research and personalize the salutation and agency name correctly. A mismatched or generic cover letter signals lack of effort and causes immediate dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author platform and subject-matter credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Essential: author activity establishing themselves as experts in their fields (for nonfiction). Examples include being a go-to source for journalists, interviews in magazines/newspapers/blogs/TV, and maintaining a clean, professional website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show demonstrable expertise and visibility. Don't propose prescriptive books in fields where you lack relevant credentials or experience (anti-pattern: 'Don't write a prescriptive health book if you are a landscaper').

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete marketing plan (not boilerplate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Biggest faux pas: including a marketing section that reads, 'Author is willing to participate in publisher’s promotional efforts.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a specific, substantive marketing/platform plan. Generic willingness to promote is inadequate; list platforms, contacts, media experience, and concrete promotional strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age-group and format interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency has represented every age group but is currently taking on very few picture books and is especially interested in middle-grade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When querying, note the agent’s current interests within children’s publishing (e.g., middle-grade preferred now) and avoid sending picture books unless solicited.
